Oct 27 : Robinhood Markets reported a drop in third-quarter profit on Tuesday as slower cryptocurrency trading weighed on growth, despite robust trading activity across other asset classes, sending its shares down 3.4 per cent after the bell. Crypto markets have come under pressure this year amid heightened volatility and persistent outflows, as inflationary pressures and higher interest rates make bonds and other traditional investments more attractive than speculative assets. Meanwhile, tensions in the Middle East tensions rattled global markets during the quarter, spurring trading activity on brokerage platforms as investors adjusted portfolios and hedged against risks. Robinhood's transaction-based revenue rose about 19 per cent to $867 million, driven by strength in equities, options and prediction markets. The Menlo Park, California-based company posted a profit of $476 million, or 51 cents per share, for the three months ended September 30, compared with $556 million, or 61 cents per share, in the year-ago period.

Source: Reuters

Oct 27 : Visa reported a jump in fourth-quarter profit on Tuesday as customers swiped their cards to pay for travel, shopping and dining out. US consumer spending has remained resilient in the face of persistent inflationary pressures, underpinned by a strong labor market and wage growth. The FIFA World Cup, which ran from June 11 to July 19, also helped boost activity across Visa's network as it brought many visitors to the United States. Payments volume, a gauge of consumer and business spending on Visa's network, jumped 9 per cent in the quarter. The world's largest payment processor's net income was $6 billion, or $3.19 per share, in the three months ended September 30, compared with $5.1 billion, or $2.62 per share, a year earlier.

Source: Reuters

ZURICH, Oct 27 : Logitech International on Tuesday reported a better-than-expected profit for the second quarter, with the computer mouse and keyboard maker seeing higher demand for its gaming and video conferencing devices. The Swiss-U.S. company reported non-GAAP operating income of $231 million for the three months to the end of September, beating forecasts for $204 million in a consensus gathered by Visible Alpha and the company's own guidance for $185 million to $210 million. Sales rose 3 per cent to $1.22 billion, in line with analyst forecasts and towards the upper end of the company's own outlook of $1.19 billion to $1.22 billion. Logitech said the growth was driven by strong performance in the United States, as well as video collaboration and gaming products, while profit margins also rose as the company achieved a more favourable product mix and faced lower import tariffs into the US.

Gaming products, which include racing wheels, microphones and mice adapted for computer game players, increased sales by 8 per cent, helped by the launch of 15 new products during the period. Sales of video collaboration equipment rose 12 per cent as business customers refreshed their workplaces after encouraging staff back to the office. Logitech also said it had suffered a lower-than-expected impact from the forced closure at a factory of one of its semiconductor suppliers earlier this year, which it originally expected to cost it $200 million in lost sales in the next quarter. After finding other suppliers the company said it now expects the impact to be $70 million to $80 million. The factory reopened in September, with full production expected to be resumed by the end of 2026. As a result, Logitech said its sales would be in the range of $1.36 billion to $1.43 billion for the three months to the end of December. It also expects non-GAAP operating income of $220 million to $255 million down from $312 million a year earlier, due to higher component and transport costs, as well as the lost sales caused by the factory shutdown.

MADRID, Oct 27 : Barcelona's pursuit of Julian Alvarez came at a modest cost on Tuesday after the Spanish FA fined the club €602 ($672) following a complaint by Atletico Madrid over contact with the striker. Atletico accused Barcelona of approaching the Argentine, whose contract runs until June 2030, without first notifying them in writing. The sanction falls under Article 133 of the federation's regulations. Atletico also complained to FIFA, which declared it had no jurisdiction over the case. For Alvarez, the repair work has been rather more public.

LOS ANGELES, Oct 27 : UPS CEO Carol Tome told Reuters on Tuesday the AI data center boom is a decades-long opportunity for the world's largest parcel delivery and logistics company, which aims to boost profits by handling fewer, but more premium, shipments.   Global data center spending is estimated to hit roughly $1 trillion in 2026 and more than double before the end of the decade as tech giants like Alphabet, Microsoft, Meta and Amazon invest billions of dollars in artificial intelligence facilities, which require significant new electricity infrastructure to power and cool servers and computer chips.  The logistics opportunity associated with data centers is $15 billion per year, said Tome.  "It is from manufacturing floor to front door," she said. UPS is flying in critical components such as advanced microprocessors, arranging ocean shipments for equipment of all shapes and sizes, warehousing goods and delivering parts to project sites.

Tome spoke after UPS raised its annual revenue and profit forecasts on better-than-expected third-quarter earnings. Data center projects have become divisive as communities weigh job creation and economic growth against electricity prices, water use and noise. Investors separately are questioning companies' massive investments in them. Nevertheless, there are many projects underway and once those are built, there will continue to be demand for parts and equipment to keep them running, Tome said. "This is something that's going to be decades," Tome said of demand. While UPS data center revenue is growing quickly, it has not yet matched revenue from its healthcare segment, which hit $3 billion in the latest quarter, Tome said, declining to give a figure for the newer business. INFLECTION POINT As part of Tome's "better, not bigger" growth strategy, UPS has been reconfiguring its network to be smaller, nimbler and more profitable.  It has consolidated facilities to reduce costs and improved service quality by investing in things like temperature sensors as well as package scanning and tracking. It also has focused on high-growth and high-margin segments like healthcare, returns and, most recently, data centers.   UPS has made significant headway in specialized healthcare logistics, shipping temperature-controlled chemotherapy drugs, cancer treatments and direct-to-consumer GLP-1 weight-loss drugs. It is now the largest player in the $148 billion global healthcare market after some key acquisitions and internal growth.    That business generated revenue of $6 billion for UPS in 2020 and is forecast to reach $13 billion in revenue this year, Tome said.   UPS is racing rival FedEx for the same high-margin volume as they each wean off low-margin to unprofitable deliveries of online purchases and other goods. FedEx, which has set up a dedicated team to court data center-related business, will report quarterly results after the market close on Wednesday. Meanwhile, retailers like Amazon.com  and Walmart as well as growing rivals like OnTrac are aggressively targeting domestic shipments in certain parts of the country. Some of that includes volume UPS and FedEx don't want.  UPS has cut doorstep deliveries of millions of packages for Amazon that it considered unprofitable, which helped lift its margin. Tome said the margin would keep improving every year. "We've moved through an important inflection point," Tome said.

Source: Reuters

Oct 27 : Lazio maintained their unbeaten start to the season and moved provisionally top of the Serie A standings with a 6-2 win at Sassuolo on Tuesday in a frantic game where the hosts had a player sent off and the visitors had two penalties saved. Gennaro Gattuso's Lazio side have eight wins from nine games and are on 25 points, three ahead of Inter Milan, who visit bottom club Venezia on Wednesday. Lazio, backed by a sizeable away support, roared into a second-minute lead through Kenneth Taylor but the game had barely restarted following a lengthy VAR check when Kristian Thorstvedt equalised. Lazio looked in control with quick goals from Gustav Isaksen and Romano Floriani Mussolini before Sassuolo's hopes of a comeback took a hammering just after the half-hour mark when Thorstvedt was shown a red card for a foul on Mattia Zaccagni.

Zaccagni spurned a chance to score again shortly after the interval when Simone Cinquegrano's handball gave Lazio a penalty, but the captain's tame spot kick was saved by Stefano Turati. Lazio found a fifth goal with Tijjani Noslin's curled shot from outside the box before a foul by Duje Caleta-Car on Isaksen gave the visitors another penalty, and this time Turati saved from Davide Frattesi. Noslin again made up for Lazio's wastefulness from the spot with another strike from distance to complete the scoring as Gattuso's side continue to look like real title contenders.

FAST

MEXICO CITY, Oct 27 : Ferrari fans can only imagine what might have been had local boy Kimi Antonelli signed for their team rather than Mercedes as a young go-karter. Formula One's oldest and most successful team had the chance to secure the talent now set to become Italy's first champion in 73 years, and Formula One's youngest ever, but let it slip through their fingers. Mercedes seized the opportunity instead in 2018, when Antonelli was 11. "For Ferrari, Kimi was still too young whereas Mercedes could offer better guarantees regarding his future prospects," Antonelli's former manager Giovanni Minardi told the Gazzetta dello Sport newspaper earlier this year.

Former Ferrari president Luca di Montezemolo, who was no longer involved with the team at that point, saw a silver lining. "I am a Ferrari man but I'm delighted to see what Antonelli is doing," he told Spanish newspaper AS last month. "What I do regret is that Ferrari had the chance to sign him. They didn't. "A great opportunity vanished, but almost better for Antonelli. Such a young Italian driving a Ferrari... It would have been terrible pressure." Mercedes team boss and co-owner Toto Wolff credited Gwen Lagrue, who is joining Red Bull next year to run their young driver programme, for bringing Antonelli, now 20, on board. He said also that people did not appreciate the amount of work that has gone into nurturing the team's successor to seven-time world champion Lewis Hamilton. "I read an interview with Piero Ferrari last week where he said, 'What a talent. He reminds me of Niki Lauda'. And I'm thinking, 'People don't get that this is the work of nine years'," the Austrian told reporters after Antonelli won last Sunday's US Grand Prix in Austin, his ninth win of the season. "The development of nine years, the hardship of nine years, the integration of the team, the working with the engineers, the 10 or more millions spent in the development of his career, of his ability, of his character together with his parents. "It's just not that it landed like this." Wolff recalled how others said Antonelli, after nine rounds without points last year, should not have been given the Mercedes seat.  He spoke of those at other teams who suggested the youngster should not even be in Formula One. "All of that now is extremely satisfying, to see what he's able to deliver and how he's working with the team, with (race engineer Peter) Bono (Bonnington) and yielding the results. But it wasn't an easy road."

Source: Reuters

NEW YORK, Oct 27 : The US Federal Election Commission's website has been targeted by a hacker or hackers, disrupting the agency's electronic filings system a week before the November 3 elections, according to an email seen by Reuters. In a statement, the FEC said that, "at this time, the FEC’s electronic filing system is currently offline and our IT staff are actively working to restore service." The FEC, which tracks the spending of candidates and political committees, said that users could still search the website for past reports. It declined further comment on the outage. The hacking attempts come a week before the midterm elections, which will determine whether President Donald Trump's Republicans maintain their majorities in Congress for the next two years.  The FEC does not play a role in administering US elections and the outage should have no effect on voters' ability to cast ballots.

"The result is there will be less disclosure on the elections" until it's fixed.  A status message posted by the FEC noted that its filing system had been down since around 10 p.m. ET on Monday (0200 GMT Tuesday). Oct 27 : The Federal Communications Commission said Tuesday it has approved Amazon Leo’s $11.5 billion deal to acquire Globalstar as the retail giant's satellite arm aims to build a satellite-based communications network to take on Elon Musk's SpaceX Starlink unit. Amazon Leo has launched more than 300 satellites since April 2025 and aims to deploy about 3,200 satellites in Earth's low orbit by 2029. Through the deal, Amazon adds Globalstar's two dozen satellites to its existing network of more than 200 and its mobile-satellite spectrum. Amazon, which has committed to investing more than $10 billion in Leo, is preparing to roll out its commercial satellite services by the end of 2026, the FCC said. The FCC said the companies’ assets will boost Amazon Leo’s entry into the direct-to-device market and allow the satellite-operator to offer fixed and mobile services. "The FCC has empowered Amazon Leo to deliver fast, next-gen satellite broadband services, increase competition, and help communities stay connected all across the country," FCC Chair Brendan Carr said.

Direct-to-device satellite technology allows smartphones and other devices to connect directly to satellites. Tech companies are pouring billions of dollars into capturing the lucrative market for satellite-based connectivity as they race to complete with Starlink's network of more than 11,000 satellites. The FCC will vote Thursday to advance a new auction of wireless spectrum to boost "direct-to-device" services. Globalstar currently powers satellite-based safety features such as Emergency SOS and Find My for Apple's iPhone and Apple Watch users. Amazon said earlier that it has signed an agreement with Apple to continue providing those services. Apple invested about $1.5 billion in Globalstar in 2024 to fund the expansion of its iPhone communication services, in a deal that also gave the tech giant a 20 per cent equity in Globalstar. Apple accounted for about 63 per cent of Globalstar revenue last year and Amazon plans to acquire Apple's stake, the FCC said. CAPE TOWN, Oct 27 : Fast bowler Mitchell Starc did not know Australia’s premier batsman Steve Smith would not take part in the decisive third test against South Africa at Newlands on Tuesday until he went to warm-up ahead of play. Smith tested his neck injury in the nets on Tuesday morning but was still experiencing discomfort, captain Pat Cummins said at the toss. "He wasn't happy with how his neck was feeling, so we had to look elsewhere," Cummins said. Smith's absence meant he would not feature at the ground where he was embroiled in the 2018 ball-tampering 'Sandpapergate' scandal, with much of the pre-match focus centred on how Australia's most experienced batsman would cope with the occasion.

"I did not know he was not playing until I went out to warm-up today," Starc told reporters after the day’s play. “He has been battling that neck since last week. “I don’t actually know what happened with that and I have not asked. He seems upbeat enough, but I don’t know what he has had done.” After winning the toss, Cummins opted to bowl, a rare decision at Newlands that might have been taken with the reshuffle of the top six batsmen after Josh Inglis learnt just before the start he would replace Smith.   The move initially appeared to have backfired as South Africa made a strong start. However, Starc produced a masterful spell with the second new ball late in the day, finishing with figures of 6-72 as the hosts were dismissed for 329 on the stroke of stumps. “I am not in that pay bracket,” Starc said when asked if he agreed with the decision to bowl first. “My opinion doesn’t matter. It is what it is. At one point it looked like we were bowling a fair bit tomorrow, so it was good to bowl them out today. “There was clearly not as much swing and sideways movement as we thought might be on offer (early in the day). But we found different ways to be effective and if you delete that first session, I think the last two were back on what we expected.” It was another see-saw day in a series that has already seen plenty of twists and turns. “These are two very good cricket teams. At times it is going to get away from you, at times you will wrestle the momentum back, which we did in the second half the day,” Starc said. “I expect more swings through the test match as we now need to go and bat and they have a very good (bowling) attack.”

Oct 27 : San Francisco 49ers tight end George Kittle said the team will carry the sting of their first loss of the season into their bye week, a mood he believes could help sharpen a battered roster that have built their identity around physical football. The 49ers returned from Atlanta disappointed with their 29-20 loss to the Falcons on Sunday but encouraged by the prospect of getting several injured players back after the break, Kittle told Reuters in a Zoom interview on Monday. "Losing is not fun," Kittle said. "But it is really hard to win in football. Everybody's a professional, everybody's talented." But he said the defeat could give San Francisco a needed edge during the now 6-1 team's time away from the field.

"Instead of, 'Hey, we're going on this bye week, we're just going to go enjoy ourselves, forget about everything,' you're kind of sitting there angry for the entire week," Kittle said. "And I think that'll be good for our football team." MOUNTING INJURIES The loss came as San Francisco have been hit hard by injuries, particularly at wide receiver.  Kittle said the team had effectively lost all of their training-camp receivers, an unusual strain on an offense that has relied heavily on its remaining playmakers. Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel were among those who were unavailable on Sunday but expected to return in Week Nine.  Still, the veteran tight end said the 49ers' depth — especially contributions from recent draft classes — has bolstered his confidence that the team can contend for a championship. "We have young players who are out there making plays," Kittle said, pointing to rookies and younger players rotating along the defensive line and contributing elsewhere on defense. "We don't have to win every game on the shoulders of Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey, or Nick Bosa and Fred Warner." VIOLENT GAME  The injuries, Kittle said, are partly an unavoidable consequence of how San Francisco play. "We pride ourselves on playing a very violent game of football," he said. "When you turn on our tape, our whole offense, we're running off the ball, we're hitting people, we are blocking. Our defense is flying around, hitting people as hard as they possibly can." That approach creates wear and tear over a long season, he said, but it is not something the 49ers intend to change. "We sit on violence, and that's the way that we think football should be played," Kittle said. "I wouldn't change how we play because that's what makes us us." Kittle pointed to the 2021 season as an example of a San Francisco team overcoming early injuries. The 49ers started that year 2-4 before winning eight straight games to reach the playoffs and advancing to the NFC Championship Game. INJURY COMEBACK This season has also presented a personal challenge for Kittle, who said he spent most of the close season recovering from an Achilles injury. Rather than his usual summer regimen of route-running and blocking work, he said his rehabilitation consisted largely of calf raises for months. Kittle said he did not return to practice until shortly before the team's trip to Australia to open the season, leaving him little time to regain football conditioning before playing again. "I definitely felt a lot of rust early on," he said. "But the more that I play, the more that I practice, the more I'm starting to feel like myself again." He said he has felt closer to full football condition over the past two weeks. "When something like that's taken away from you, it hurts," Kittle said. "But it also lights a fire in you every single day." CANCER SCREENINGS Away from the field, Kittle is working with Novartis on a prostate-cancer awareness campaign built around blood-test screening. Kittle said the partnership resonated because his grandfather had prostate cancer and survived it before later dying. He said he was struck by learning that one in eight men will be diagnosed with prostate cancer and that early detection can substantially improve outcomes. "The point is to make it comfortable," Kittle said, adding that many men are reluctant to discuss screening. "You literally just go get a blood test. It's so much easier and it's not daunting." For now, though, Kittle said the 49ers will take an unhappy break and use it as motivation for the stretch ahead. "I'll be pretty grumpy," he said. "I know I'm a positive guy, but I get grumpy too sometimes."

Source: Reuters

NEW YORK, Oct 27 : A US regulator is investigating whether prediction market operator Polymarket violated a 2022 enforcement deal in which it promised to ban US users from its main overseas platform, reviving an inquiry the agency shuttered last year without bringing charges, said two people familiar with the matter. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is probing whether Polymarket took sufficient steps to keep US users off the platform as part of a broader investigation it opened into the company earlier this year, the people said. One of the people said the scrutiny is focused on Polymarket's past controls and processes. The agency is examining Polymarket's controls for determining where customers are located, as well as its advertising activities in the United States, as part of that inquiry, the people said. Polymarket is based in New York and has an offshore entity registered in Panama.

The CFTC is also scrutinizing Polymarket's US platform, which the company began rolling out late last year, including its customer onboarding processes and customer protections, said the people, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss confidential enforcement issues. Reuters is reporting these elements of the probe for the first time. The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg News and other media first reported in June that the CFTC was broadly probing Polymarket, but provided few details. Bloomberg added that the CFTC was looking into social media activity tied to the company. Spokespeople for the CFTC and Polymarket declined to comment. Probes are not necessarily an indication of wrongdoing and many do not result in enforcement action.  The new details, nevertheless, raise fresh questions over why the CFTC and Justice Department last year closed similar probes into whether Polymarket had violated the 2022 settlement, which resolved CFTC allegations at the time that Polymarket had been operating in the US unlawfully since its launch in 2020.  Neither agency has commented on the decision to close the probes and a Justice Department spokesperson declined to comment for this story. Prediction markets allow traders to bet on real-world events, including sports, government policy announcements and elections. Aided by supportive policies under President Donald Trump's second administration, the industry has surged over the past two years. Trump's son, Donald Trump Jr, is a Polymarket investor.  As the platforms have grown, they have drawn scrutiny from Democratic lawmakers and advocacy groups worried the platforms are creating new avenues for insider trading, while recent political upsets, including in Brazil this week, have raised questions about their accuracy. Polymarket has said it has revamped controls. The firm says it expressly prohibits the use of virtual private networks (VPNs) or similar tools to circumvent its geographic restrictions, and has extensive controls to monitor for misconduct and to prevent restricted users from accessing its offshore platform.  Speaking to Reuters in August, Shana Bautista, Polymarket's global head of investigations and intelligence, said US users circumventing its restrictions was not "a really prevalent issue."  BIDEN ADMINISTRATION AGENCIES OPENED PROBE IN 2024 Under the 2022 settlement negotiated by the CFTC's former Biden-era leadership, Polymarket agreed to stop offering its market to US users. But as 2024 US election bets on the platform grew, political pundits and social media users questioned whether Americans were circumventing Polymarket's restrictions.   Months before the election, the CFTC opened a probe into whether Polymarket was complying with the deal, Reuters and other media reported at the time. The Justice Department opened a related investigation, with the FBI searching Polymarket CEO Shayne Coplan's New York home in November 2024. Two months later, the Trump administration took office and appointed new leaders to both agencies. On July 15, 2025, Coplan said in an X post that the CFTC and Justice Department had closed their probes and cleared the company of any wrongdoing. A week later, Polymarket said it had bought a CFTC-licensed derivatives exchange, which became the platform for its US operation. CFTC-registered platforms must comply with certain customer protection and market abuse prevention requirements. While CFTC data shows the agency's overall enforcement activity has slumped during Trump's second presidency, its enforcement director David Miller said during his first month on the job in March that he would aggressively police prediction markets.  In April, the agency and Justice Department charged a US soldier, alleging he made $400,000 from insider bets on Polymarket's offshore platform, sparking fresh questions about its controls.  According to the indictment, Gannon Ken Van Dyke, who has pleaded not guilty, accessed the platform using a VPN and "exit mode," which geolocated to a foreign country. Polymarket said at the time that it had referred the matter to the authorities.

Source: Reuters

VATICAN CITY: Pope Leo will meet with survivors of sexual abuse by Catholic clergy during his Nov 6 to 17 three-country tour of South America , the Vatican said on Tuesday (Oct 27). Leo , who is recovering from lung cancer surgery , will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on one of the most intense foreign trips taken by a pope in decades, after being deemed fit for the journey by his doctor on Monday. "Several meet ings are planned with people who have been victims of abuse by members of the clergy and the Church," the Vatican said in its Tuesday statement. "These meet ings reflect the pope 's desire to express his closeness to those who have suffered, and who still suffer, because of this violence," it said. Leo , 71, has held meet ings with survivors of abuse by clergy on several of his foreign visits, including in France last month. In that encounter, the pope met for two hours with seven French victims and reaffirmed his commitment to ending abuse of children by Catholic priests, the Vatican said afterwards. Leo , originally from the US, served as a missionary and bishop in Peru for decades before becoming pope .
